newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Resolute to combine milling to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Resolute to combine milling to cut costs.

text.p: Resolute Ltd said on Wednesday combined cash production costs at its Higginsville and Chalice gold mines in Western Australia would decline under a plan to jointly process ore from both mines.

Resolute chief executive Michael Carrick told Reuters that by closing its ore mill at Higginsville and trucking the ore 30 km to the mill at the Chalice mine, cash costs at Higginsville will decline by over A$100 an ounce.
"Studies show we will be able to drop cash costs there in excess of A$100 an ounce," he said.
Combined cash costs from both mines would average around A$230 an ounce, Carrick said.

Cash costs in the most June quarter at the Chalice mine declined to A$183 an ounce, among the lowest in Australia, from around A$250 an ounce previously, due to mining of a high-grade zone, Carrick said.
Cash costs at Higginsville have been averaging about A$500 an ounce, making it one of Australia's highest cost mines.
Production from the two mines will be about 140,000 ounces a year, Carrick said.
Carrick said the mill at Higginsville would probably be deployed to Resolute's 50 percent owned Challenger gold project, located in South Australia's Gawler Craton region.
